source: DS-Agent (Guo et al. 2024) Automated data science with LLMs and CBR
finding: An LLM agent retrieves a human-insight case, revises the plan from execution feedback (ReviseRank plus Revise loop), and retains successes. The deployment stage adapts a past solution with only minor edits.
numbers: 30 data-science tasks. Development, 12 tasks: GPT-4 100% success. Deployment, 18 tasks, one-pass rate: GPT-3.5 85%, GPT-4 99%; best baseline 56% and 60%. Mixtral-8x7b-Instruct 6% to 31%.
limits: Cases are human Kaggle write-ups; deployment tasks come from the same distribution as the stored solutions. Mostly tabular tasks.
agent_relevance: Strongest LLM-era support that editing a retrieved solution (O7) works when the case is close and execution feedback is available.

source: DS-Agent ablation on the revise loop and on CBR
finding: Removing the feedback-driven revise of the retrieved case hurts; removing CBR hurts more.
numbers: Average best rank over 12 development tasks, GPT-4, five trials (lower is better): full DS-Agent 2.08; w/o ReviseRank 2.58; w/o CBR 3.41.
limits: Rank metric only; no confidence intervals in the table. Small task set (12).
agent_relevance: Feedback-driven adaptation of the case is worth about half of the CBR gain here. Keep an execute-and-revise step after retrieval.

source: DS-Agent: case form and number of cases (Fig. 6)
finding: Homogeneous cases (a task plus one of its solutions) beat heterogeneous textual insights. Adding more cases to the context made performance fall quickly; zero cases was worst.
numbers: Case number swept in the deployment stage; zero-shot was poorest; performance declined rapidly as retrieved cases increased. Exact values are only in a figure.
limits: Figure-only numbers. Authors call the decline unexpected versus ordinary few-shot learning.
agent_relevance: Retrieve few cases (1 to 3) of the same shape as the target; do not stuff the context.

source: DS-Agent cost of the CBR setting
finding: Adapting a stored solution is much cheaper than building from scratch.
numbers: Dollars per run: development GPT-3.5 $0.06, GPT-4 $1.60; low-resource deployment $0.0045 and $0.135.
limits: Cost figures are the authors' own accounting.
agent_relevance: Supports a cheap reuse path (edit a case) as the default, and a costly path only on failure.

source: TextBFGS (Zhang et al. 2026) CBR code optimisation via error-operator retrieval
finding: Cases store abstract error-to-operator corrections (how a fix was made), not code. The system retrieves by error feedback, applies the operator to the current code, and retains successful adaptations.
numbers: Abstract: +20.5% pass rate on MBPP and -50.6% tokens on HumanEval vs TextGrad-based baselines; +16.2% on MBPP cross-domain. Test sets are tasks where Qwen3-235B-A22B scored 0 at Pass@1: HumanEval-Hard 45 tasks, MBPP-Hard 117 tasks.
limits: Hard subsets chosen by failure of the same base model; one base model; Python only.
agent_relevance: Store the edit operator, not only the old answer. Good fit for O7: a case should carry a transformation.

source: TextBFGS ablation (Tables 1 and 2)
finding: The case base adds a lot; retrieval by error beats retrieval by problem.
numbers: HumanEval-Hard Plus pass: TextGrad 82.22, Momentum 86.67, TextBFGS w/o case base 82.22, problem-retrieval variant 93.33, full TextBFGS +2.22 over that variant. MBPP-Hard Plus pass: TextGrad 48.72, Momentum 58.12, w/o case base 48.72, problem-retrieval 74.36, TextBFGS 78.63.
limits: Table columns in the extracted text were scrambled; only values stated in prose or on unambiguous rows are used. Single run, no CIs.
agent_relevance: A case base lifts a hard subset from 48.7 to 78.6 Plus pass; large effect but on a filtered failure set.

source: TextBFGS cross-domain transfer of adaptation cases (Tables 3 and 4)
finding: Problem-similarity retrieval overfits surface features; error-pattern retrieval transfers across datasets.
numbers: Problem-based retrieval, MBPP tasks with HumanEval cases: Plus pass 58.12 (no-case baseline 48.72), a 20.51 point drop from in-domain 78.63. Error-based retrieval, same cross setting: 74.36, which is +16.24 over problem-based. In-domain HumanEval, problem-based slightly better (97.56 vs 96.34).
limits: Only two datasets; both Python function synthesis.
agent_relevance: Index adaptation cases by the type of difference or failure, not by topic. Matches classic adaptation-guided retrieval.

source: TextBFGS token cost
finding: A case base at equal pass rate cut tokens.
numbers: TextBFGS without case base matched TextGrad at 82.22% Plus pass with 18.4% fewer tokens (reported 25.2k for the comparison arm). Best setting saved 50.6% of total tokens (21.6k).
limits: Token counts are totals over the hard subset.
agent_relevance: Adaptation from a case can save calls, not only raise accuracy.

source: Nguyen et al. (2026) CBR-to-SQL: two-stage retrieval then Revision
finding: Stage 1 retrieves examples by masked question structure; stage 2 (Revision) aligns entities to the database schema. Compared with single-step RAG.
numbers: MIMICSQL AccEX/AccLF: CBR-to-SQL 0.894/0.862 vs RAG-to-SQL 0.860/0.825. EHRSQL AccEX 0.895 vs 0.818, AccLF 0.729 vs 0.676. Ablation (MIMICSQL): no Revision stage 0.786/0.776; replacing Proposal with plain retrieval 0.889/0.851.
limits: Single preprint. Healthcare text-to-SQL only.
agent_relevance: Removing the explicit adapt step cost about 11 points; the smarter retrieval was worth only about 0.5 point. The edit step carried the gain.

source: CBR-to-SQL brittleness to removing top retrieved examples
finding: When top-ranked cases are removed, the system with an explicit adaptation stage degrades less.
numbers: Drop in AccEX (lower is better): MIMICSQL 0.028 (CBR) vs 0.074 (RAG); EHRSQL 0.043 vs 0.138.
limits: A second table in the paper shows smaller gaps (EHRSQL AccEX 0.086 vs 0.171; AccLF 0.182 vs 0.184).
agent_relevance: A good adapt step lets a weaker neighbour still work; less reliance on near-exact matches.

source: DomAgent (Wang et al. 2026) KG plus CBR retrieval for domain code
finding: Combines knowledge-graph retrieval with case retrieval so the LLM adapts a retrieved example to a domain library.
numbers: DS-1000 pass@1: GPT-4o 51.0%, GPT-4o with DomRetriever 58.6% (+7.6). A Qwen2.5-7B variant reaches 96.64% on a proprietary truck CAN-signal task vs 39.62% vanilla; one model goes from 71.22% to 98.04% with DomRetriever.
limits: Truck task is proprietary; retrieval tool trained with RL on 300 DS-1000 samples. Pairing of baselines in the truck table only partly read.
agent_relevance: Retrieval plus adapt helps most when the model lacks domain knowledge.

source: Memento (Zhou et al. 2025) ablation: planning versus case memory
finding: Case-based memory gives additive gains on top of planning on three benchmarks. A small memory beats a large one.
numbers: Case memory gains (F1/PM): HLE +4.5/+7.0, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2. Retrieved cases K in {0,2,4,8,16,32}: best at K=4 (F1 64.5, PM 78.5), flat or slightly lower for larger K.
limits: Cases are state, action, reward triples used as guidance; adaptation is left to the planner LLM and not isolated. Contamination flagged on DeepResearcher.
agent_relevance: Retrieval size near 4; do not expect more cases to help.

source: Memento headline results
finding: Non-parametric or Q-learned case retrieval for a planner LLM, no weight updates to the LLM.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6 F1 and 80.4 PM; SimpleQA 95.0 PM; case memory adds 4.7 to 9.6 points on out-of-distribution tasks.
limits: Planner GPT-4.1 with o4-mini or o3 executors; many moving parts.
agent_relevance: A deployed agent loop whose reuse step is retrieve then adapt in context.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows from past trajectories and injects them as guidance, which the model adapts to the new task. Gains held on a cross-template WebArena subset.
numbers: WebArena (gpt-4) total success 35.5% vs BrowserGym baseline 23.5%; abstract: 51.1% relative gain on WebArena and 24.6% on Mind2Web.
limits: Self-induced workflows depend on judged success; many WebArena tasks share templates, hence the cross-template subset.
agent_relevance: Abstracting a case into a workflow before reuse makes later adaptation easier.

source: Sourati et al. (2023) CBR with language models for logical fallacies
finding: A retriever, an attention adapter that fuses the new case with k retrieved cases, and a classifier. Improves over vanilla LMs.
numbers: CBR beat vanilla baselines by 2.5 to 6 absolute F1 points in domain and up to 8 out of domain, and beat few-shot Codex. Performance peaked at one retrieved case and fell as k grew to 5.
limits: Trained adapter on small LMs (ELECTRA among them); not a prompting-only LLM.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as DS-Agent and Memento: one or two well-chosen cases.

source: Sourati et al. case representation and what the adapter uses
finding: How a case is represented changes results; retrieved labels are barely informative.
numbers: Representation changes F1 by 6 to 8 points in domain and 4 to 8 out of domain; counterargument enrichment strongest for ELECTRA. Overlap of retrieved labels with true labels about 27.7%, only slightly above a frequency baseline.
limits: Suggests the adapter extracts abstractions, not labels.
agent_relevance: Gains from cases may come from high-level structure, not copying. Write cases with abstract structure.

source: Ye, Zhao, Leake, Wang, Crandall (2021) Case difference heuristic with deep features
finding: Learns a network that predicts solution difference from problem difference (CDH), on face-age regression. Adaptation usually improves the retrieved solution.
numbers: Mean abs error in years, normal setting: constant 12.94; regressor 5.97; L1 retrieve 9.58 then adapt 8.14; Siamese retrieve 7.49 then adapt 7.86 (worse). Novel ages above 70: regressor 32.77; L1 35.84 to 32.11; Siamese 33.05 to 28.83.
quote: Adaptation-guided retrieval might be a way to alleviate this problem.
limits: Image regression, not text. In distribution the plain regressor wins.
agent_relevance: Adaptation helps most when the query is far from stored cases; it can hurt when the case is already close.

source: Ye et al. (2021): retrieval and adaptation out of sync
finding: Retrieval tuned for closeness plus adaptation trained on random pairs gave worse answers after adaptation. The paper cites Leake and Ye 2021 for the explanation and an alternating-optimisation fix.
numbers: Siamese + adaptation, normal setting: MAE rose from 7.49 (retrieved) to 7.86 (adapted). In every novel-age setting adaptation reduced error (for ages 50-70: 14.85 to 12.02).
limits: Single dataset and task.
agent_relevance: Test the adapt step on near neighbours too: it may do harm there. Gate adaptation on distance.

source: d'Aquin, Badra, Lafrogne, Lieber, Napoli, Szathmary: CABAMAKA case base mining
finding: Mines pairs of cases for adaptation rules (frequent closed itemsets), validated by an expert, in breast cancer treatment.
numbers: n = 647 cases, 2344 frequent closed itemsets in about 2 minutes, 208 kept (change in both problem and solution properties).
limits: Semi-automated and expert-checked; no accuracy figure in the part read.
agent_relevance: Old AI route to adaptation knowledge: learn rules from case differences. LLM analogue: derive edit rules from solved pairs.

source: Badra, Cordier, Lieber (2009) Opportunistic adaptation knowledge discovery
finding: Calls adaptation the Achilles heel of CBR. Triggers adaptation-knowledge mining at problem-solving time, when a case needs it.
numbers: No accuracy numbers in the abstract.
quote: Adaptation has long been considered as the Achilles' heel of case-based reasoning
limits: Method paper.
agent_relevance: Learn the edit rule when the failure appears (lazy), not up front.

source: Hanney and Keane (1996) Learning adaptation rules from a case base
finding: Original case difference heuristic: attribute the difference in solutions to the difference in problems and form rules. Seen only as described in Ye et al. 2021 and d'Aquin et al.; the paper was not opened.
numbers: Per d'Aquin et al.: the CBR system with learned adaptation outperformed the one without adaptation in their experiments (no figures seen).
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Founding method for learned adaptation.

source: Olausson et al. (2024) Is self-repair a silver bullet for code generation?
finding: Repair of one's own output depends on feedback quality. Gains are modest once repair cost is counted; a stronger feedback model helps a lot.
numbers: Code Llama 13b, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 on HumanEval and APPS. Human feedback (16 participants, 40 failing GPT-4 programs, 2 feedbacks each, 25 repairs sampled per pair) raised GPT-4 repair success 1.58x overall. Table 1 cells: 42.64% to 62.21% and 19.33% to 45.67%.
limits: Small human study; Python with unit tests. Which table cell is which difficulty level was not recoverable from the extracted text.
agent_relevance: Any revise step needs a diagnosis step. Plain edit-it is weak; give the editor an error signal.

source: Huang et al. (2024) LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet
finding: Without external feedback or oracle labels, self-revision does not help and often hurts.
numbers: GSM8K: GPT-3.5 75.9 standard, 75.1 after round 1, 74.7 after round 2; GPT-4 95.5, 91.5, 89.0. CommonSenseQA GPT-3.5: 75.8, 38.1, 41.8. HotpotQA GPT-3.5 26.0, 25.0, 25.0. With oracle labels GSM8K GPT-3.5 reaches 84.3.
limits: Intrinsic self-correction only; with a verifier results differ.
agent_relevance: An adapted answer must be checked by an outside test; unaided rewriting of a retrieved answer is risky.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Prompt the model to recall three relevant problems with solutions before solving: self-generated retrieval and reuse.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo GSM8K: 0-shot 75.0, 0-shot CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated exemplars 77.8. MATH: 33.0, 33.9, 34.9, 37.3.
limits: Gains are a few points. On PaLM2 GSM8K the self-generated result (81.7) beat 5-shot (80.7). Code generation needed an added high-level knowledge step.
agent_relevance: A one-prompt substitute for a case library when none exists; the gain is small.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Case-based or rule-based: how do transformers do the math?
finding: Fine-tuned transformers solve basic arithmetic by case-based interpolation from nearby training cases and fail inside a left-out square. Rule-following fine-tuning fixes it.
numbers: Random split reaches 100% accuracy; accuracy drops inside the held-out 441-sample square and falls as its side grows (10 to 40). Rule-following fine-tuning: Llama-2-7B 91.1% at 9-digit addition vs scratchpad under 40%; GPT-3.5 over 95% at 12 digits from 100 training samples.
limits: Fine-tuning study, not prompting; arithmetic only.
agent_relevance: Models reuse nearby cases but do not apply rules to far cases; far cases need explicit rules.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG for legal question answering
finding: RAG with legal cases as context and hybrid embeddings; the LLM is the adapter.
numbers: Cosine score vs reference: no RAG 0.8967; best hybrid AnglE-BERT with k=3, 0.9141, about a 1.94% gain; better than No-RAG at 95% confidence.
limits: High no-RAG baseline from parametric knowledge; metric is embedding cosine, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: Small measured gain from case context with unaided adaptation.

source: Pang et al. (2026) CAST case-based calibration for LLM tool use
finding: Uses historical execution cases as signals for reward design and reasoning length in RL, framed as case-based adaptation.
numbers: Up to 5.85 points gain in execution accuracy on BFCLv2 and ToolBench; average reasoning length down 26%.
limits: Trains the model with RL, so not a pure scaffold. Only abstract and intro read closely.
agent_relevance: Weak link: cases tune the reasoning budget, not the edit of a solution.

source: Review of CBR for LLM agents (2025)
finding: Describes adaptation in LLM agents as transformational (substitute, delete, insert), compositional (merge parts of several cases) and generative (synthesise guided by cases), chosen by a meta-cognitive step. Lists case adaptation as an open challenge.
numbers: No new measured adaptation experiment found in the text read; it restates DS-Agent (100% development success, 99% one-pass) and the fallacy work.
limits: Conceptual survey; taxonomy not tested.
agent_relevance: Useful vocabulary for O7: choose substitute, merge or regenerate by how far the case is from the target.

source: Leake and Ye (2021) alternating optimisation of retrieval and adaptation
finding: Cited in Ye et al. 2021 as explaining why independently trained retrieval and adaptation can make adapted answers worse, and proposing alternating training. Paper not opened.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Tune retrieval and adaptation together.

source: Search status note: LLM adaptation coverage 2020-2026
finding: WebSearch quota and the arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned HTTP 429 this session, so no systematic sweep was possible. Not found: a head-to-head test isolating an LLM adapt step against retrieval alone, apart from the DS-Agent and CBR-to-SQL ablations.
numbers: None.
limits: Gap, not evidence.
agent_relevance: Our own ablation (retrieve only vs retrieve plus edit) would be new evidence.
